sliceagent.review:
Issues found in the `miniweb` package:

- `miniweb/validators.py` — `clamp()` returns `high` for almost all inputs because `min(n, low)` and `max(high, ...)` are inverted.
- `miniweb/response.py` — `finalize()` sets `Content-Length` to `len(self.body)` (characters), not UTF-8 bytes, so non-ASCII bodies get an incorrect length.
- `miniweb/request.py` — `__init__` uses a mutable default `params={}`, so separate `Request` instances can share the same params dict.
- `miniweb/router.py` — `match()` uses substring matching (`route in path`), so e.g. `/foo/admin/bar` incorrectly matches a route registered as `/admin`.
- `miniweb/auth.py` — `header()` lookup is case-sensitive, but HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so `Authorization` may be missed.
- `miniweb/auth.py` — Logs the raw bearer token at INFO level, leaking credential material.
- `miniweb/auth.py` — Token comparison uses `==`, which is vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks.
- `miniweb/auth.py` — `replace("Bearer ", "")` only strips a literal, case-sensitive prefix and does not require it, so raw or oddly prefixed tokens are accepted.
- `miniweb/cache.py` — Cache key is only `request.path`, ignoring method, query params, and headers; POST/DELETE responses can be cached/served for GETs and per-user responses can leak across requests.
- `miniweb/cache.py` — The in-memory cache is unbounded with no eviction, allowing memory exhaustion under load.

extra_claims.claim: Bearer token extraction via replace('Bearer ', '') only strips a literal, case-sensitive prefix and does not require the prefix, allowing raw or oddly prefixed tokens to be accepted.
Cache key ignores HTTP method and headers (in addition to query params), allowing POST/DELETE responses to be served for GETs and per-user responses to leak across requests.
The in-memory cache is unbounded with no eviction, allowing memory exhaustion under load.
